title: Adaptive Cost Advisor: governance, verification and fast-revert runbook for batching/caching recommendations
creator: Maya Chen
summary: After an incident where the automatic batching/cache advisor applied a configuration that increased tail latency for small interactive workloads, this ticket captures the incident follow-ups: a governance checklist, automated verification steps, a fast-revert runbook, and a test harness for future recommendations.
incident_timeline: 2025-02-12: Optimize Advisor rollout 2025.02 applied adaptive batching rules to 'chat-lite' route in us-west-2 (canary 10%).
2025-02-12 09:12 UTC: Post-deploy telemetry showed 5% increase in 95th percentile latency for 'chat-lite' measured across synthetic and real traffic within 30 minutes.
2025-02-12 09:40 UTC: Pager alert (SLO-regression) triggered; oncall routed traffic back to previous policy manually.
2025-02-12 11:00 UTC: Initial rollback completed; incident declared mitigated.
root_cause: The Adaptive Cost Advisor's heuristics favored larger batch sizes for mid-length prompts to reduce token cost. The policy lacked a route-specific latency regression check and applied change during a 10% canary without verifying tail-latency under small-traffic burst patterns. An untested interaction between KV-cache TTL and batching window widened request coalescing, increasing queueing for low-concurrency bursts.
findings: Advisor lacked route-specific QoS constraints—global cost objective overrode per-route latency SLOs.
Canary gating checked mean latency and token-cost but not P95/P99 under traffic burst profiles used by chat-lite.
KV-cache TTL change had been staged in the same recommendation batch; combined effect not simulated in preflight tests.
Runbook for automatic revert existed but required manual approval due to safety flags—delaying revert by ~28 minutes.
Telemetry dashboards did not surface combined effect of batching+cache changes in a single pane; debugging required correlating three dashboards.
No synthetic workload that reproduces low-concurrency burst patterns was included in the advisor CI suite.
short_term_mitigations: 1) Add an immediate fail-safe to block Advisor recommendations that change both batching and cache TTL for the same route in a single rollout.
2) Tighten canary gating to require P95 and P99 checks for routes with <100 qps but high SLO sensitivity.
3) Create an automated revert action that can be triggered without human approval when SLO regression > threshold within canary window.
4) Add an alert that correlates batching policy changes and cache TTL updates so oncall sees combined changes in one timeline.
5) Backfill synthetic test that reproduces low-concurrency burst scenarios into Advisor preflight suite.
long_term_actions: Governance: introduce a recommendation schema that declares per-route QoS constraints (latency SLO, max tolerated increase, cost target) and require Advisor to respect it.
Verification: extend preflight harness to run 'micro-burst' synthetic traffic and record P90/P95/P99 impacts for candidate configs.
Observability: build a single-pane diff view showing token-cost delta, mean latency, P95/P99, and queueing metrics for the pre/post simulation and live canary.
Orchestration: implement a fast-revert API that can be called by PagerDuty runbooks and by the Advisor itself when predefined guardrails trip.
Testing: add combined-change simulation tests (batching + cache + kv-ttl) to CI with deterministic seeds for reproducible profiles.
Policy: require 'change-impact' annotation for multi-parameter recommendations (explains expected cost delta and latency risk).
runbook_fast_revert: Scope: apply when canary P95 increases >10% or absolute increase >50ms for routes with interactive SLOs.
Step 1: From Console -> Recommender -> Active Canaries, locate 'chat-lite' canary entry and click 'Abort & Revert'.
Step 2: If UI unresponsive, run CLI: redwoodctl recommend revert --canary-id=<CANARY_ID> --reason='SLO-regression'.
Step 3: If CLI fails, call orchestration API: POST /v1/internal/recommendations/<REC_ID>/revert with service token (ops key).
Step 4: Verify revert: wait for replication, then query metrics: prometheus query 'redwood_route_p95_latency{route="chat-lite"}' and confirm value returned to baseline within 2 canary minutes.

Step 5: If revert cannot be applied within 15 minutes, open emergency rollback: scale down new pool instances by removing policy binding via redwoodctl scale policy --policy=<POLICY_ID> --scale-to=0 and route traffic to pre-policy pool.
Step 6: Post-mitigation: tag the recommendation as 'failed' and block identical recommendation variants for 7 days. Add incident tag and link to the postmortem.
automation_spec: Preflight suite additions: synthetic 'micro-burst' generator, 3 randomized seeds, durations 30s/60s/120s, verify P95/P99 impact <= threshold.
Canary gating rules: require pass on mean latency, P95, P99, and request queue depth for the target route; all checks must pass to promote beyond 10% canary.
Advisor behaviour: if a recommendation touches multiple knobs (batching, cache, kv-ttl), split rollout into staged sub-changes unless explicit approval is present.
Auto-revert policy: automated trigger threshold (P95 increase >10% OR P99 increase >20% OR queue_depth increase >2x) during canary window triggers immediate revert action.
test_plan: Create a synthetic workload generator for 'chat-lite' that reproduces the 08:00-09:00 user burst pattern recorded on 2025-02-12.
Add CI job 'advisor-preflight-e2e' that runs candidate recommendations through the simulation and uploads artifacts to S3 for manual review.
Run an extended canary (1 hour) for combined changes with automated check that P95/P99 remain stable; include a stage for human approval only if metrics stable.
Set up nightly regression job that replays past incident traffic traces and validates advisor recommendations against them.
decision_log: 2025-02-18: Steering committee chose to prioritize safety gates over aggressive cost wins for Q1 (decision recorded in Confluence: /confluence/Optimize/Safety-Decision-2025-02-18).
2025-02-25: Agreed to implement automated revert API and to add multi-condition canary checks. Assigned to backend team for March sprint.
2025-02-27: Design reviewed single-pane diff; UX adjustments requested to surface queueing metrics more prominently (see design PR #412).

postmortem_notes: Primary lesson: Cost-focused heuristics must be constrained by explicit per-route SLO metadata; without that, automated systems will surface regressive changes under certain traffic shapes.

Operational lesson: The time-to-revert was extended by manual approval gates that were intended to be safety checks. We will split gating responsibilities and provide an emergency automatic path for strict SLO-regressions.
Engineering lesson: Testing for combined parameter interactions is easy to miss; CI must include combinatorial grid samples for cost/latency affecting knobs.
Communication: Improve incident-first documentation so PMs and Product Ops can quickly classify advisor failures as cost vs reliability and choose escalation path.
notes: This ticket should be coordinated with the SRE rotation and consulted with Compliance if the fast-revert API requires elevated tokens.

Client-facing communication draft: 'We discovered an automated cost-optimisation change that had unanticipated latency effects for lightweight chat traffic. We reverted the change and have added additional safeguards to prevent recurrence.'
